job-title: Braze a replacement section of suction line
job-setting: Residential split system, condenser on the side of the house next to landscaping. Leak found on the suction line.

line 1: Marcus
Refrigerant's recovered into the recovery tank, gauges are reading zero. Cutting out the leaking section with the tubing cutter.

line 2: Marcus
Deburring the cut ends and cleaning them up with sand cloth till they're shiny.

line 3: Marcus
Fitting the new section and coupling in. Gonna skip flowing nitrogen, the bottle's way out in the truck and it's just one joint.

line 4: Marcus
Coupling's seated all the way on both ends, and the pipe's supported so nothing shifts while I heat it.

line 5: Marcus
Unit's tight against the hedge here, kinda dry and crunchy, but I'll be quick. No need for the extinguisher, we're outside.

feedback-text: Right moment to stop. Here's the problem: A brazing torch easily ignites dry vegetation. Hot work requires clearing or shielding combustibles and having an extinguisher in reach. Here's the right way: Clear or wet down the area, put up a heat shield or blanket, keep an extinguisher within reach, and keep a fire watch after.

line 6: Marcus
Lighting the oxy-acetylene torch, bringing the fitting up to a dull cherry red.

line 7: Marcus
Service valve's only a couple inches from this joint. Not gonna wrap it, it's a fast braze.

line 8: Marcus
Feeding the fifteen percent silver rod, letting it draw into the joint all the way around.

line 9: Marcus
Joint's cooled. Pressure testing with nitrogen and it's holding steady.

line 10: Marcus
Pulling a vacuum down below five hundred microns and doing a decay test before charging.
result-summary: Caught 1 of 3 mistakes · 0 false alarms

missed-list: MAJOR · MISSED · -75 PTS

Brazing without flowing nitrogen. Copper scale broke loose, clogged the TXV screen, and the system came back two weeks later starving for refrigerant.

Should have: Flow nitrogen at a few CFH through the line while brazing to displace oxygen.

MINOR · MISSED · -25 PTS

Didn't protect the nearby service valve from heat. The valve's seals cooked and it started leaking at the stem, so the job had to be redone with a new valve.

Should have: Wrap the valve with a wet rag or apply heat-blocking paste, and remove the Schrader core before brazing.
